finding: Norwegian survey: pacing rated useful by 96%, rest 97%; 79% of those with graded training said it worsened health; 57% found cognitive-challenge help useful.
note: Self-selected members of patient organisations; no control group

population: ME/CFS ("pure" CFS without sleep/mood disorder, Fukuda-type)
n: 32 CFS vs 30 sleep apnoea vs 14 controls
finding: Polysomnography: CFS showed increased slow-wave sleep, lower sleep efficiency and higher microarousal index than controls; NREM distribution differs from sleep apnoea, so not a primary sleep disorder.
38% of teenage girls with CFS/ME scored above the anxiety cut-off; anxiety symptoms were not associated with school attendance or disability.
Incremental exercise in CFS: lower baseline ascorbate and Hsp70, early larger TBARS rise, no IL-6/TNF rise and blunted Hsp27/70 responses, reduced M-wave.
Exemplar patient-journey service framework document for children with CFS/ME; no data.
Occupational guideline on fitness for work in CFS; summarises limited evidence on employment outcomes.
Psychiatric diagnosis (SCID) present currently in 57% and lifetime in 89% of population-identified CFS cases vs 45% and 79% in insufficient-symptoms group; few had seen mental health specialists.
note: Psychiatric comorbidity does not establish cause

finding: Each 1-point allostatic load index increase raised the odds of CFS by 26% (OR 1.26, 1.00-1.59) vs well controls, with a gradient well < ISF < CFS; fatigue duration inversely correlated with ALI.
Four-week inpatient graded exercise programme: VO2peak +17% (p=0.01), time to fatigue +18%, fatigue severity -13% and depression -42%.
note: Uncontrolled case series, short follow-up, no PEM measures

finding: Patients at biologically vs psychosocially oriented clinics differed in onset type, attribution, pain and education but not fatigue, age or psychopathology.
Parents of adolescents with CFS overestimated their child's IQ more than control parents.
No difference in IL-6, sIL-6R or sgp130 at rest or after exercise; F2-isoprostanes higher at rest and after exercise; only lactate-threshold power lower.
Patients who kept expended energy within perceived available energy improved in physical function and fatigue severity in a post-hoc analysis of a trial.
note: Post-hoc, self-reported energy quotient, groups not randomised

finding: Graded-activity CBT: self-reported improvement in 9 of 11 but actigraphy increased in only 3, decreased in 4, unchanged in 2.
Three activity-pattern instruments (API, IPAQ, CFS-AQ) had fair validity against actometers (AUC 0.64-0.71) with many misclassifications.
Muscle biopsies showed a shift from slow to fast-twitch fibre proportion in CFS, with preserved single-fibre force, velocity and calcium sensitivity.
Pet ownership (58%) was not associated with fatigue, GHQ-12 or SF-36 scores.
Small heart on chest X-ray was common in CFS; echo showed small LV chamber and poor cardiac performance, which fluctuated with symptom severity across repeated exams.
note: No control group in abstract; Fukuda-type criteria likely

finding: Case report: complement split products positive for 14 months in a post-EBV CFS patient, who then recovered.
24-h ambulatory BP: CFS had lower systolic blood pressure and abnormal diurnal regulation vs controls, with a fatigue comparison group (PBC) included.
Premorbid personality (TCI): lower novelty seeking, higher harm avoidance and persistence in CFS.
Open pilot of antibiotics for presumed Chlamydia pneumoniae infection in psychosis, with two CFS patients added; reports good outcomes.
Illness intrusiveness correlated with fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, disability and depression in 24 ME patients.
CFS patients scored higher on harm avoidance and persistence (TCI).
Parvovirus B19 DNA found in gastric/intestinal biopsies in 40% of CFS vs <15% of controls; HHV-7 common in both; EBV and HHV-6 in 15-30%.
note: Same gut-biopsy approach as Chia enterovirus work; unreplicated

finding: Large CFS sample showed clear cognitive impairment on an extensive battery, independent of psychopathology.
note: Sample size not given in abstract

finding: Vis-NIR spectroscopy of thumb: lower water, higher oxyhaemoglobin and more oxidised cytochrome c oxidase in CFS, read as faster blood flow and energy metabolism.
note: Unvalidated technique, resting thumb only; finding opposes tissue under-perfusion

finding: Review hypothesising that HPA hypofunction in CFS reflects a dysregulated stress system with a cytokine-driven sickness response.
Lifestyle (smoking, diet, BMI) of CFS patients was no worse than the Dutch population on weight and alcohol; unhealthy factors were not associated with fatigue or impairment.
CDC-criteria prevalence 2.1% (London) vs 1.6% (Sao Paulo), p=0.20; diagnosed in 11 British cases but none in Brazil.
German review of fibromyalgia, CFS and interstitial cystitis overlap with IBS, proposing central hypersensitisation.
Four weeks of a multi-strain probiotic: no change in fatigue or activity; neurocognitive scores improved; gut flora unchanged; 6 of 15 reported improvement.
Practice nurses had limited CFS/ME knowledge and some held sceptical views, a barrier to primary care management.
Neutrophil "ATP profile" mitochondrial indices correlated with Bell scale severity (p<0.001); 70 of 71 patients outside the normal region.
note: Commercial proprietary test, unclear methods, possible conflict of interest

n: 21 CFS vs 20 thyroid disease vs 21 healthy
finding: CFS group had impaired memory, attention and visuo-construction; attention deficit remained after controlling for mood.
Patent application for anti-CD20 antibodies in CFS/ME; no data.
Plasma CoQ10 significantly lower in ME/CFS (p=0.00001); 44.8% below the lowest control value; inversely related to fatigue and autonomic symptom scores.
note: Plasma CoQ10 deficiency not in atlas; unreplicated; speculative mortality claims

finding: Hypothesis paper proposing kindling and oxidative stress as unifying mechanisms.
Urinary 8-OHdG (creatinine-adjusted) was higher in patients with both depression and ME/CFS than controls and other groups; correlated with FF scale.
note: ME/CFS alone not elevated per abstract; urine marker

finding: Fatigue and somatic symptoms in depression form a dimension separate from the depression factor.
IgM anticardiolipin antibodies found in 95% of CFS sera.
note: No control numbers in abstract; unreplicated

finding: Childhood trauma associated with 6-fold increased CFS risk; low salivary cortisol response to awakening found only in a CFS subgroup with trauma.
Short review noting sexual dysfunction (low desire) in women with CFS and scarce data.
About 70% of patients were moderately or severely depressed; coping styles related to appraisals of illness severity.
Bayesian analysis of CDC SNP data found NR3C1 in significant gene-gene and gene-gender interaction models.
note: Reanalysis of old candidate-gene data; no replication

finding: Walking at preferred speed was slower in CFS (0.84 vs 1.19 m/s) and the physiological (oxygen) cost of walking was higher than controls.
Thesis description on beliefs, deficits and predictors of recovery; no results in abstract.
FTIR of fingernails showed lower alpha-helix and higher beta-sheet protein content in CFS.
note: Unreplicated exploratory technique (same Japanese group as thumb Vis-NIR)

finding: Over 2 years, self-reported improvement tracked with momentary fatigue and standing time; actigraphy change correlated with physical function; <20% reached healthy range.
NICE 2007 guideline CG53 on diagnosis and management of CFS/ME (later replaced by NG206).

population: Rat food-restriction plus forced swimming model

finding: Review of microarray work: 88 differentially expressed genes (85 up); qPCR clustering gave seven subtypes with different SF-36 scores and severity.
note: Reviews the authors' own earlier work; unreplicated

finding: After treadmill exercise, PBMC HSP27 baseline higher in CFS and fell below baseline up to 7 days; HSP60 fell in CFS but rose in controls.
note: Very small sample; opposite baseline direction to Jammes 2009 (low Hsp70)

finding: Sleep EEG spectral power did not differ between CFS twins and their healthy co-twins; sleep EEG features were more genetic than disease-related.
DSM personality disorder prevalence was 12% in CFS, same as the general population (psychiatric 54%).
Depression mediated the fatigue-disability relationship in CFS.
Children with CFS/ME scored below norms on sustained, switching and divided attention and auditory learning.
62% attended 40% of school or less; school attendance linked to physical function (OR 1.70) not to anxiety.
Integrated gene co-expression network analysis found a 299-gene module linked to CFS severity and 20 candidate genes.
note: Methods paper on CDC microarray data; no external validation of biology

finding: Meningococcal B vaccination as a teenager not associated with CFS/ME (adjusted OR 1.06, 0.67-1.66).
Energy index point score correlated with fatigue severity score (r=0.67).
Diurnal salivary cortisol output rose after 15 sessions of CBT alongside clinical response, suggesting hypocortisolism is potentially reversible.
MSLT sleep latency was shorter in CFS than controls but within normal range; CFS had less objective sleepiness than sleep apnoea and higher fatigue.
US train-the-trainer education program reached 2064 primary care providers.
36% of self-reported CFS respondents were depressed; 22% of depressed had considered suicide.
Network analysis integrating gene expression and neuroendocrine data showed rewiring around pituitary and thyroid nodes in CFS.
Blood microarray: CD19+ B-cell gene set lower in CFS (p=0.01; PTPRK, TSPAN3); co-expression suggested inflammatory signalling.
Both CFS and MDD patients had fine motor slowing vs controls on copying tasks.
Active stand test: max heart rate higher in CFS/ME (106 vs 98 bpm, p=0.02); POTS in 27% (16/59) vs 9% of controls (p=0.006).
Lower frequency of the IL-17F His161Arg (rs763780 C) allele in CFS patients vs controls.
Principal components separated psychological symptoms from a physical-symptom/functioning/fatigue component; functional incapacity tracked physical symptoms.

n: 11 CFS vs controls; validation 3 + 20, then 18 CFS + 12 non-CFS
finding: Nine-gene blood expression set (incl. GZMA, ATP5J2, COX5B, STAT5A) classified 94% of CFS and 92% of non-CFS fatigue patients in a final PCR set.
note: Small, no independent replication, classifier optimism

finding: Dutch and French kinesiophobia and symptom list questionnaires showed good reliability.
Implemented CBT: 37% recovered; costs fell and the programme was cost-saving from a societal view.
31P-MRS during low-intensity exercise: ADP-PCr recovery kinetics were normal in CFS/ME (mitochondrial regulation intact), but lost in primary biliary cirrhosis.
note: CFS/ME is only the fatigued comparator, n=8

finding: During incremental exercise, CFS reached exhaustion sooner (351 vs 715 s) with lower prefrontal oxygenation (HbO2, HHb, tHb, TOI) and lower max HR.
Proposes post-radiation syndrome as an NO/ONOO- cycle CFS-like illness.
Cochrane review: CBT vs usual care reduced fatigue (SMD -0.39, 95% CI -0.60 to -0.19; 6 studies, 373 participants).
note: Subjective outcomes, unblinded trials, Oxford/Fukuda populations

finding: CANTAB: CFS had slower motor speed and impaired spatial working memory and recognition versus controls after excluding psychiatric disorders and cognitive drugs.
A considerable number of CFS patients had a small heart on chest X-ray (cardiothoracic ratio).
Interviews show physicians draw on social and cultural knowledge to understand CFS/ME.
CFS group showed attentional bias to health-threat stimuli.
At baseline CFS had lower grey matter volume; after CBT grey matter increased in lateral prefrontal cortex, related to cognitive speed.
note: Small; atlas notes no consistent structural MRI difference; no untreated control follow-up in abstract

finding: Low-dose dexamethasone suppression: basal cortisol was raised and overall suppression did not differ (80% vs 76%); only the comorbid-depression subgroup (n=9) hypersuppressed.
note: Small subgroup, atypically elevated basal cortisol

finding: Serum IgM to nitro-BSA was higher in CFS, partial CFS and MDD than controls (highest in CFS) and correlated with IgM/IgA to gut-bacteria LPS.
Over-ground gait differed in CFS at self-selected speed (slower, p=0.002); when speed matched, patterns similar except at the ankles.
Health care use in CFS was predicted by fatigue and perpetuating beliefs such as symptom focus; tertiary patients used more specialist care.
Patients reported disbelief, psychologising by doctors and worsening with prescribed activity.
Polysomnography: CFS had less total sleep, lower efficiency and less REM than controls; unrefreshing sleep linked to poor sleep efficiency and short sleep runs.
Higher daily energy quotient (expended/perceived energy) was associated with worse fatigue, pain, depression, QoL and disability.
High pre-infection stress index predicted CFS/ME 1-3 years after symptomatic parvovirus B19 (OR 25.7, 1.7-121.9).
Walk limited by heart rate at RER 1.0 raised fatigue immediately that returned to baseline at 24 h; pain stayed elevated; 6 of 24 felt worse.
Sensory amplification related to physical functioning via pain intensity, independent of depression.
fMRI during imagined fatigue: CFS had more occipito-parietal/posterior cingulate and less prefrontal activation than controls; reverse pattern with anxiety scenarios.
Hypothesis that CFS is caused by a circovirus entering the brain.
Polysomnography transition statistics: fewer REM-to-non-REM transitions and more REM/stage-I-to-wake transitions in CFS.
Estimated annual direct cost per patient of $2,342 (community) and $8,675 (tertiary); total cost to US society about $18.7-24 billion.
88 genes differentially expressed in blood (85 up); qPCR clustering gave 7 subtypes with different SF-36 scores and severity.
Awareness of CFS was 16.2% in Brazilian vs 55.1% in British primary care attenders; 30.8% of Brazilian specialists named CFS for a vignette.
Arterial stiffness (AIx@75) was greater in CFS (22.5 vs 13.3%, p=0.002), with higher CRP and isoprostanes, correlating with CRP and oxidative stress.
Narrative argues graded exercise with self-management and pacing can be done safely without immune harm.

population: CFS in 1946 British birth cohort (self-reported diagnosis)
finding: Prospective cohort: CFS (1.1%) was not preceded by more childhood illness or atopy; higher childhood/adult exercise frequency and lower BMI preceded later CFS.
Flattened diurnal cortisol: lower morning and higher evening salivary cortisol in CFS; IL-6 highest in CFS but not significant after BMI adjustment.
25% had asynchronous breathing; one breathing retraining session lowered respiratory rate and raised tidal volume acutely.
HRQoL much lower than norms; 63% had clinically significant psychological distress; physical fatigue and symptom frequency best predictors.
2.1-year follow-up of CBT RCT: fatigue gains maintained; physical function and school attendance rose further.
Narrative review of traditional Chinese medicine for CFS; no pooled data.
Serum B19 DNA cleared within 4-5 months in all 18 tested; complement levels persistently lower in patients with persistent symptoms.
Three HTR2A polymorphisms (-1438G/A, C102T, rs1923884) associated with CFS and with disability and fatigue measures.
Head-up tilt: orthostatic intolerance in 13 CFS vs 5 controls; POTS without hypotension in 7 CFS and no controls; sympathetic predominance in HRV.
Implemented CBT had effect sizes comparable to RCTs, 32% early dropout.
15-week diary: CFS reported more upper respiratory infections; stress preceded infections and fatigue.
Children under 12 (16%) were as disabled as older children (school attendance about 40%); 24 of 26 also met CDC criteria.
Patent for anti-CD20 antibodies in CFS; no data.
IPA of interviews identified six themes on symptom perception and diagnosis.
Illness intrusiveness mediated the effects of symptoms and impairment on depression.
Thesis on illness cognitions of significant others of CFS patients; no results in abstract.
Chinese paper distinguishing sub-health state from CFS and reviewing definitions.
Narrative systematic review arguing CFS is often misdiagnosed as depression and underdiagnosed (>80%).
Review of Chinese acupuncture/moxibustion studies: all reported 79-100% response but quality was poor and none was randomised.
Recall of fatigue exceeded momentary ratings, related to catastrophizing and depression.
Thesis on emotional expressivity and attitudes in relation to social and home functioning.
Salivary cortisol deviation from the expected diurnal pattern was associated with higher fatigue and pain.
Art-making was linked to increased well-being among women with CFS/ME.
Weekly recall of fatigue was higher than momentary diary ratings but moderately to highly correlated.
Larger Th2-memory shift related to poorer sleep and higher basal salivary cortisol.
IPA interviews showed identity loss, scepticism and acceptance themes.
RNase L cleavage, RNase L activity, PKR and elastase activity intercorrelated and related to daily functioning.

n: 328 CFS sera plus 17 CCFP, 8 GWV, 24 PC, 52 normal
finding: Ciguatoxin-antibody titre of 1:40 or more in 91% of 328 CFS sera; anticardiolipin IgM in about 88-90% of 41 tested; claims "acute phase lipids" related to mitochondrial cardiolipin.
note: Unvalidated assay, nonspecific antibody binding likely

finding: Attenuated morning salivary cortisol profile in CFS, limited to women (not men).
Higher resting HR, diastolic BP, norepinephrine and epinephrine; exaggerated cardiovascular response to LBNP, attenuated response to handgrip.
Seven gene-expression subtypes mapped to clinical phenotypes; subtypes 1, 2, 7 most severe, subtype 6 post-exertional.
Serum IgM against phosphatidyl inositol raised in CFS and depression vs controls and partial CFS; correlated with fatigue and depression.
note: Very small, same group as nitro-BSA IgM

finding: Actigraphy: longer total sleep and lower activity vs controls; irregular and delayed sleep phase patterns.
Recombinant CMV early-antigen immunoassay detected IgM in 11.8% vs 2.2% by ELISA in CMV IgG-positive patients, claimed as active CMV infection in a CFS subset.
note: No control group, case definition unclear

finding: Corrected QT interval short in CFS (372 ms) vs FM (417 ms); positive hemodynamic instability score distinguishes CFS from FM during tilt.
note: No healthy control group in abstract; short QTc not in atlas

finding: PSQI subjective sleep quality poorer in CFS while polysomnographic sleep efficiency and slow-wave sleep did not differ.
note: Contradicts same group's earlier SWS finding

finding: Psychiatric illness at ages 15-36 was associated with later self-reported CFS/ME (OR 2.65, 1.26-5.57), dose-response.
CBT vs controls reduced fatigue (d=0.48); mean dropout 16%.
Grounded theory of self-renewal amid contested illness.
Pain catastrophizing related to bodily pain (r=-0.70) and exercise capacity (r -0.41 to -0.61).
Alexithymia prevalence 30% in CFS adolescents; only identifying-feelings subscale higher; no effect on recovery at 1.5 years.
Scoping review: no risk factor was replicated in more than two studies; none suitable for identifying at-risk patients.
Disabled Gulf veterans were more likely to meet CFS criteria than similarly disabled non-Gulf veterans (adjusted OR 7.8, 2.5-24.5).
Lower salivary cortisol responses after dexamethasone and CRF in CFS, mainly in patients without early-life stress.
Methods paper on gene-ontology pathway analysis of CFS expression data.

Blood counts normal; CFS had lower RDW, higher MPV, neutrophils and N/L ratio; reduced overnight urine output and amino acid excretion (asparagine, branched-chain, succinate lower; 3-methylhistidine, tyrosine higher).
Meta-ethnography: legitimacy doubts and disbelief challenge patient identity.
CFS publication output did not rise 1995-2004 while FM and fatigue output did.
PBMC COX-2 and iNOS production higher in CFS and correlated with severity and NF-kB.
PBMC NF-kappa B p50 production higher in CFS (p=0.0002 unstimulated) and correlated with severity.
Mitogen-induced CD69 expression on T and NK cells was lower in CFS (AUC about 89%), no difference in cell counts.
note: Sample size not in abstract; unreplicated

finding: Ecological momentary assessment after maximal exercise: physical symptoms worsened only after a five-day delay in CFS; cognition and mood unchanged vs controls.
note: Small; delay longer than atlas typical

finding: Resting PetCO2 low overall; imagery of hostile resistance lowered PetCO2 with poor recovery and more hyperventilation complaints.
COMPASS autonomic symptom score >32.5 had PPV 0.96 and NPV 0.84 for CFS in validation; symptoms correlated with fatigue.
Higher baseline norepinephrine, epinephrine, HR and temperature; abnormal skin blood flow and vasoconstriction thresholds during hand cooling; more thermoregulatory symptoms.
Fatigued twins had worse motor function, processing speed, verbal memory and executive function; sudden onset linked to slower processing; depression did not explain it.
Estimated CFS prevalence 2.54% in adults 18-59, with female:male ratio 11.2:1 metropolitan but 0.8:1 rural.
note: Higher estimate than other studies; empirical criteria

population: CFS and breast cancer fatigue women
finding: Focus groups: similar core symptoms of fatigue, neurocognitive and mood problems in cancer-related fatigue and CFS.
Written information to GPs about CBT for CFS increased referrals and knowledge.
CFS prevalence in Nigeria somewhat higher than US community-based estimates.
After a 4-hour sleep delay, CFS twins had less slow-wave activity in the first NREM recovery period than their co-twins.
Short German review of FM and CFS in children.
Cold pressor pain threshold and tolerance did not differ significantly between CFS twins and co-twins, but subjective pain and fatigue ratings were higher.

population: CFS (adults and adolescents; CBT RCT data)
finding: CBT reduced self-reported cognitive impairment but did not improve reaction time or symbol-digit performance.
Maximal exercise test: relative peak VO2 z-score -1.13 (p=0.002) but absolute peak VO2 not significantly reduced; peak HR and BP below reference.
Pain fell in CBT-recovered patients relative to non-recovered; higher baseline pain predicted poor outcome.
fMRI during fatiguing working memory task: mental fatigue related to cerebellar, temporal, cingulate and frontal activity; CFS had greater activity in several regions.
IPA: women felt disbelieved, then took self-help and gained control through social support.
Patent for CFS diagnosis from blood mRNA expression of marker genes; no data in abstract.
Multiple NR3C1 (glucocorticoid receptor) SNPs associated with CFS and fatigue measures; major-allele homozygotes OR 2.61-3.00.
Over 4-6 months, incidence of chronic fatigue syndrome 0.5%; prognosis good; anxiety/depression at baseline predicted chronic fatigue.

population: Focal brain lesions (MS, encephalopathy) with chronic fatigue

finding: 5 mg prednisolone suppression test: lower salivary cortisol pre-dose and higher percent suppression in CFS, indicating enhanced negative feedback.
Two-night PSG: prolonged sleep latency, low sleep efficiency, low slow-wave sleep; alpha-delta intrusion correlated with anxiety, not RNase L or immune parameters.
8-min stand test: abnormal orthostatic tests in 53% vs 20% controls; orthostatic hypocapnia identified a subgroup of CFS.
note: Analysis restricted to 62 patients/35 controls with clear results

finding: Submaximal VO2 predicted peak VO2 (r=0.70) with mean error 14.6%; not accurate for individual use.
Discourse analysis of how ME/CFS is constructed as serious, enigmatic and not psychological.
Pragmatic non-randomised group CBT study using waiting-list controls; results truncated.
After CBT 69% no longer met CDC criteria; 23% fully recovered by the strictest definition; comorbid conditions lowered recovery.
Alexithymia not associated with momentary fatigue or pain ratings.
LORETA EEG: higher delta in left uncus/parahippocampal and higher theta in cingulate and right superior frontal gyrus in CFS twins.
Active HHV-6 (mostly variant B) and HHV-7 reactivation found in CFS only; dual infection more frequent; lower CD3+/CD4+ in dual-active patients.
Patients on antidepressants (especially SSRIs) recovered faster and held gains at 3 years, versus untreated patients.
Polysomnography/MSLT: sleep architecture did not differ except more obstructive apnoeas per hour (not clinically meaningful); 18% vs 7% severe primary sleep disorders (ns).
note: Population-based; conflicts with other PSG studies

population: Chronic unexplained disabling fatigue clinic patients
finding: Patients retrospectively rated themselves more active before illness than controls rated themselves 2 years earlier.
Erythrocytes in CFS: raised 2,3-DPG and oxidative damage markers with stomatocytes on electron microscopy, linking redox to red cell shape.
Most families named infective causes; rest and activity reduction were favoured management.
Acceptance related to less fatigue and distress.
Childhood trauma associated with 3- to 8-fold higher CFS risk, graded with exposure.
HADS had a 3-factor structure in CFS and web administration inflated scores.
n-back fMRI: equal performance but CFS had greater medial prefrontal activation at low load and less dorsolateral prefrontal/parietal activation at high load.
CBT outcomes in an RCT were better than in routine care, esp. between post-treatment and 6-month follow-up.
Dutch CDC Symptom Inventory had good reliability and validity.
Updated systematic review: GET and CBT appeared to reduce symptoms in RCTs; evidence for most other interventions inconclusive.
note: Pre-2007 evidence; subjective outcomes; Oxford/Fukuda populations

finding: Incremental exercise: CFS alone had cardiorespiratory responses not different from controls and matched-fitness subgroups showed no differences; CFS+FM had lower peak VO2 and end-tidal CO2; all rated exercise more effortful.
Serum IgM against fatty acids, MDA, azelaic acid and nitro-amino acids higher in CFS than controls and correlated with severity.
note: Very small, same group as other IgM studies

finding: Positivity in illness measured at 6 and 9 months predicted mental fatigue at 12 months.
Dutch commentary: CBT and graded exercise are first-choice; calls for stepped care research.
Uncontrolled CBT/graded activity rehabilitation programme improved fatigue, disability and physical function; 70% less fatigued.
Retrospective: 58 of 99 reported symptom decrease on azithromycin; responders had lower plasma acetylcarnitine.
note: Retrospective, no control, azithromycin not in treatments index

finding: Patent for measuring glucocorticoids, sex steroids and neurotransmitters in body fluids; no data.
Patent for diagnosing CFS/ME by gene expression; no data.
24-h urinary GABA and beta-alanine excretion did not differ between CFS and controls; four patients had very high beta-alanine.
Systematic review: chronic widespread pain is disabling in CFS; prevalence poorly defined; pain threshold falls after exercise; depression not related to pain.
24-h urinary total cortisol metabolites and free cortisol did not differ between CFS and controls in either sex.
Maternal fatigue (OR 5.29) and distress (OR 5.6) were associated with CFS in the adolescent; fathers not.
Review of challenges in primary care CFS management; calls for training and self-help.
Escape-avoidance coping higher in CFS and ISF than controls; linked to fatigue and disability in CFS.
Six months of submaximal aerobic exercise with vibration improved function and strength.
Tilt with capnography: hypocapnia in 9-27% of CFS/FM/dizziness/NMS patients vs 0-2% controls; most sustained hypocapnia, not specific to CFS.
note: Hypocapnia not unique to CFS; large comparator groups

finding: Low-NK-activity CFS patients had more cognitive impairment, daytime dysfunction and worse objective cognitive scores than normal-NKA patients.
After multidisciplinary CBT/GET group treatment, retrospectively reported action-proneness increased but stayed below premorbid levels.
PBMC oestrogen receptor beta wt mRNA was lower in CFS; ERalpha and ERbeta SNPs did not differ.
Serum Vis-NIR spectroscopy with SIMCA classified 100% of healthy and 93.3% of CFS masked samples.
note: Single group, unreplicated, spectra not interpretable

finding: Patent for near-infrared spectral diagnosis of CFS; no data.
CFS-like status predicted inactive work status at 4 years (OR 3.0-4.4).
CF/CFS odds higher after mononucleosis than Campylobacter at 3 months (OR 2.77) but not 6 months; anxiety and depression strongest predictors of CF/CFS, infection type of IBS.
Narrative systematic review concluding pathophysiology unknown and recommending a biopsychosocial model; prevalence 0.2-0.7%.
CFS 1.9-fold more likely to have high allostatic load (95% CI 0.75-4.75); best discriminators waist:hip, aldosterone, urinary cortisol.
Allostatic load associated with function and symptom severity; machine-learning equations used ALI components to predict symptoms.
Microarray: 188 fatigue-related and 164 depression-related genes, 24 shared; 24-gene set separated samples by likelihood of CFS.
SNP rule ensemble predicted CFS with 76.3% accuracy (OR 8.94).
Data mining of the Wichita matrix: biological variables incl. allostatic load, sleep, HR and HRV separated cases from controls though few were significant individually.
Editorial introducing the Wichita 2-day inpatient dataset analysis issue.
Pressure-based experimental pain ratings tracked clinical pain better than heat.
Longitudinal interviews describe a pendular trajectory of identity reconstruction.
Xenon-CT: absolute cortical blood flow reduced in MCA territories in CFS (P<0.05), most in patients without psychiatric disorder.
Spanish FibroFatigue Scale had good reliability (alpha 0.88).
Corrected QT interval short in CFS supine (0.371 s) and on tilt (0.385 s) vs controls (p=0.0002).
fMRI: auditory cortex responsiveness attenuated during a fatiguing task in CFS, correlated with fatigue.
